implemented: Single-file, self-contained interactive HTML report at fasteditBench/results/compare/bench-02-report.html. Tailwind (CDN) + Chart.js 4.4.6 (CDN) + Geist font family (Google Fonts). Inline dataset (156 joined cases + per-language aggregates + overall). Zinc/Slate dark base with one accent (Electric Blue #0ea5e9). Asymmetric hero (lg:grid-cols-12 split 8/4), asymmetric three-approach column (1.2fr/1fr/0.8fr), horizontal bar headline chart, per-language clickable bars that filter the scaling scatter, and a what-we-didn't-measure definition list.
design_decisions: Stack: single standalone HTML file. No React, no build step. Tailwind + Chart.js pulled from CDN; Geist font from Google Fonts. Matches user's 'HTML page' direction and portability requirement.
Accent color: committed to Electric Blue #0ea5e9 (not Deep Rose). Zinc-950 off-black base. No lila/purple anywhere.
Typography: Geist for display, Geist Mono for numbers and labels. No Inter. No serifs.
Hero is asymmetric (lg:grid-cols-12 with 8-col headline + 4-col stacked meta block, rule-separated, no card). VARIANCE=9 tone.

Three-approach section uses fractional column widths (1.2fr / 1fr / 0.8fr) and a segmented control at the top that toggles visibility of individual approaches. FastEdit column gets a visible accent-tinted top border and a massive '0tok' numeral.
Deterministic stacked bar (76.9% accent / 23.1% ink-700) chosen over a donut — horizontal bar reads better at this aspect ratio and keeps the composition linear.
Headline chart: horizontal bar (indexAxis: 'y'), FastEdit on top as accent, Opus + GPT as neutral ink-600. The disparity is visual-first.

Per-language chart: custom HTML bars (divide-y) rather than Chart.js. Sort descending by ratio_gpt. Dual bars per language — thick accent bar for GPT ratio, thin accent-soft bar for Opus ratio. Clickable to filter the scatter.

Scaling chart: Chart.js scatter with linear regression lines per series (computed client-side in vanilla JS via least-squares). All three series shown (GPT, Opus, FastEdit) so the flat FastEdit trendline vs sloped LLM trendlines is the visual payoff.
Kinetic marquee band between hero and Section 1 — endless-scroll ticker of key numbers for a cocky-receipts vibe.
'What we didn't measure' section uses a <dl> with mono-labeled <dt> and generous body <dd> text. No cards. Honest-list aesthetic.
Motion: fade-up stagger on load via CSS cascade (--i custom property), pulse animation on a 2px accent dot, 60s marquee. All transform/opacity only. No top/left/width/height animations.
Grain/noise layer: fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none SVG turbulence at 0.08 opacity. Does not scroll with content.
Font stack includes the banned-font check via the build script itself — the output HTML was grepped for 'Inter', 'purple-', 'violet-', 'fuchsia-' before commit; zero matches.
Emoji scan: Python regex over U+1F300-U+1F9FF + U+1FA00-U+1FAFF + sun-arrow + dingbats; zero matches.
